intended_object: A recursion principle ("paramorphism") for the Clifford algebra C(Q). Given a bilinear f : M → (C(Q) × N → N) with f m (ι m · x, f m (x, y)) = Q(m) • y, and a starting value n, it is the linear map F : C(Q) → N with F(1) = n and F(ι m · x) = f m (x, F x). This comes from the docstring and the companion lemmas foldr'_ι_mul, foldr'_algebraMap and foldr'_ι.
explanation: The definition reuses `foldr` (itself built from the universal property `CliffordAlgebra.lift`) with an extended state space C(Q) × N. The auxiliary map sends (x, y) to (ι m · x, f m (x, y)). This map squares to Q(m) • id: the first component gives ι m · ι m · x = Q(m) • x, and the second component is the hypothesis hf. The definition starts the fold at (1, n) and projects onto N. On the first component the fold just rebuilds x, so the result satisfies the intended recursion F(ι m · x) = f m (x, F x), which the library proves as `foldr'_ι_mul`; it also proves F(algebraMap r) = r • n. This is the standard way to get a paramorphism from a catamorphism, and it pins down a unique linear map, since C(Q) is spanned by products of generators. It works over the same commutative ring, module and quadratic form that Mathlib's `CliffordAlgebra` needs, so it is not stated in a narrower setting. It is the general version of this construction, not a special case of something more general elsewhere in Mathlib; the only related declaration, `foldr`, is the version without the extra argument.
